Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling a smaller version of itself. To prevent the function from running forever, it must include a "base case," which is a simple stopping condition. You can think of it like opening Russian nesting dolls, where you keep opening smaller dolls until you reach the tiny, solid one in the center. Once that final stopping point is reached, the function completes each step in reverse order to produce the final result.
